record.original_question: For an open quantum billiard, let k_n denote the resonances of the Helmholtz equation (∇^2 + k^2)ψ = 0 with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Is it true that the number of resonant states satisfying Re(k_n) < k and Im(k_n) > -C grows on the order of k^(d_H+1) as k → ∞, where d_H is the partial Hausdorff dimension of the classical non-escaping set?

evidence.quote: If the billiard is open, for example consisting of a finite region containing obstacles that do not prevent the particle escaping to infinity, the Helmholtz equation has resonance solutions where k has negative imaginary part.

Open problem 15. The fractal Weyl conjecture: The number of states with Re(kn) < k and Im(kn) > −C for some positive constant C is of order k^(dH+1) where again k → ∞ and dH is the partial Hausdorff dimension of the non-escaping set.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an open two-dimensional quantum billiard: a domain Ω ⊂ ℝ² (for example, the exterior of a finite collection of compact obstacles, with Ω unbounded so that classical trajectories may escape to infinity). On Ω, study the Helmholtz equation

  (∇² + k²) ψ = 0,

with Dirichlet boundary conditions on ∂Ω. Because Ω is open, the spectrum is described by resonances: complex wavenumbers {k_n} with Im(k_n) < 0, obtained as poles of the meromorphic continuation of the resolvent (or scattering matrix) of the Dirichlet Laplacian.

Let K ⊂ Ω denote the classical non-escaping set, i.e. the set of points whose forward and backward billiard trajectories remain in a bounded region for all time (the trapped set). Let d_H denote its partial Hausdorff dimension (the Hausdorff dimension of K intersected with a Poincaré section, equivalently dim K = 2 d_H + 1 in phase space for a flow with one trapped direction).

Fix any constant C > 0 and define

  N(k, C) = #{ n : Re(k_n) < k and Im(k_n) > -C }.

Prove or disprove the following asymptotic statement (the fractal Weyl conjecture): as k → ∞,

  N(k, C) = Θ( k^{ d_H + 1 } ),

i.e. there exist constants c₁, c₂ > 0 (possibly depending on C and on the billiard) such that c₁ k^{d_H+1} ≤ N(k,C) ≤ c₂ k^{d_H+1} for all sufficiently large k.
artifact.category_tag: fractal Weyl law for quantum resonances
artifact.status_search_result: The fractal Weyl conjecture is generally regarded as still open in full generality. A fractal Weyl upper bound of order k^{d_H+1} has been proved in several settings (e.g. for open quantum chaotic maps by Nonnenmacher–Sjöstrand–Zworski, and for several convex obstacles satisfying a no-eclipse condition), and the conjecture is supported by extensive numerical evidence (three-disk scatterer, open baker's map, open kicked rotor). However, a matching lower bound — and hence the full conjecture — has not been established in general.

status_evidence.title: Fractal Weyl law for open quantum chaotic maps
status_evidence.snippet: Nonnenmacher–Sjöstrand–Zworski prove a fractal Weyl upper bound for resonances of open quantum chaotic maps.
status_evidence.claim: Fractal Weyl upper bound of order h^{-d_H} (equivalent to k^{d_H+1}) is proved for open quantum maps with hyperbolic trapped sets.

status_evidence.title: Resonance states of the three-disk scattering system
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical computation of resonances in the three-disk system extending into the deep semiclassical regime, validating the fractal Weyl law.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical evidence supports the fractal Weyl law for the three-disk billiard but a full proof remains absent.

status_evidence.title: Fractal Weyl Laws for Chaotic Open Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Lu, Sridhar and Zworski formulate and numerically test the fractal Weyl law for chaotic open systems.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture has been formulated and numerically checked, but full mathematical proof (especially lower bound) is open.
